service.description: Internal, the SECA OrderPlacedRecordAttribution's one handler (design §15.1), after an order's placement commits, in a transaction of its own: the order's admission event (order:orderId, the customer, the time placed) filed once for each active automation of its seller with the order-placed trigger, of the order's store or of every store; a failure of one automation is logged and the next goes on, and the placement never waits on it. P20: then the order's attribution (record#OrderAttribution) in a transaction of its own, so neither part's failure undoes the other or the placement; a failed attribution is logged and decided by the attribution job. Runs as the system.

The tracking links of the caller's organizations (a campaign's when marketingCampaignId names one of them, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE otherwise), current ones unless includeEnded, by text (the description or code), source, medium and type, a page at a time; each with its label and whether it is current (Sales' lead forms read the two), its campaign, state, destination in words, public URL, UTM values and non-automated clicks. Any Marketing reader (PERMISSION_DENIED for a caller who reads nothing of Marketing).

A tracking link of the caller's organizations (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE otherwise): its public URL (https://{site's canonical host}/trk/{siteId}/{publicCode}) and that URL's QR code (SVG text from the built barcode helper), its campaign, site, destination (a landing page of the organization's Marketing mount or a registered https address), safe destination, type, UTM values and dates, where it sends a visitor now, what the caller may do, and for a reader of reports or an author its observations over the last periodDays (30 by default) and in all: clicks, page visits, visitors by key, the events with no key, the recipients who clicked and the automated fetches set apart (aggregates, no person).

A new tracking link of an open campaign (marketingCampaignId) or a change of one (trackingCodeId at expectedRevision, its revision as read: STALE_REVISION otherwise), MARKETING_CAMPAIGN_EDIT in the campaign's organization (PERMISSION_DENIED, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE; a closed campaign STATUS_INVALID; a legacy code of no organization is read only). The site is one whose Marketing mount serves the organization, with a canonical host (SITE_INVALID); the destination a landing page of that organization's Marketing mount (destinationKindEnumId TdkSitePage, sitePageId) or an https address (TdkUrl, redirectUrl) on a host of a site that serves the organization or of its MarketingPolicy trackingDomains (DESTINATION_INVALID, DESTINATION_NOT_REGISTERED); the safe destination likewise; the type and UTM values the organization's current vocabulary (VALUE_INVALID). The public code is random, made once and kept.

resolveTrackingLink: where a link of a published site (its public code; a personalized token beside it) sends its visitor now: its registered destination with its UTM values while it is current, else its safe destination, else none (the neutral page); and whether the visitor key may be set (the organization's policy visitorKeys, or a recipient who allows tracking, PcpTracking). The destination comes only from the link; nothing of the request names it. An unknown code, another site's or an unpublished site is NotFound. Reads only.

recordTrackingEvent: one observation of a published site: a link's click, a page visit carrying its code or a known automated fetch (the code), or a send's pixel opened or fetched (a personalized token, no code); with the digest of the visitor's opaque key where it may be kept (the organization's policy, or a recipient who allows tracking; never the key or a party id) and the recipient only for a recipient who allows tracking (PcpTracking, checked now). Limited per client and code (30 in ten minutes) and per site (20,000 an hour); over a limit, an unknown code or token, or another site's link nothing is kept and the answer is the same (recorded false). An automated fetch is an observation, never a conversion. A TrackingCodeVisit is written beside the event when the request has a local visit.

The visits of the sites whose enabled Shop mount sells for the stores (productStoreIds, each one of the caller's Commerce stores: RECORD_UNAVAILABLE otherwise) from fromDate until thruDate: the distinct visitor keys of the non-automated tracking events plus each such event with no key. Conversion is P20's attribution.

Internal (handle#OrderPlaced after the placement commits; the attribution job): the one attribution decision of a placed sales order (MarketingOutcomeLink): the decision in force when there is one (a repeat answers it), else the most recent eligible tracking event of the order's identity (its local visit and the visitor key that visit carried, or its customer as a recipient who allows tracking now; a click or a page visit of a link of the seller, never an automated fetch or an open) within the link's trackable lifetime (30 days when it names none), else the source opportunity's campaign, else unattributed; with its evidence and evidence time, and TrackingCodeOrder beside a tracking event (never billable). An order that is not a placed sales order gets none (attributable false). Runs as the system.

A staff correction of an order's attribution: MARKETING_CONFIGURE in the order's seller organization (PERMISSION_DENIED; an order of another organization or no placed sales order RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), the decision read (expectedOutcomeLinkId; STALE_REVISION when another is in force), a campaign of the seller or none (CAMPAIGN_INVALID) and a reason (REASON_REQUIRED). The decision in force is ended, never changed, and its successor records the user, the time and the reason; the same campaign again changes nothing.

The attribution job (design §15.3): the sales orders placed in the last days (30 by default) that have no decision, at most 200 a run (maxOrders, fewer), each decided by record#OrderAttribution in a transaction of its own; an order that is not a placed sales order (a purchase order, an internal customer's) is passed over and takes no place (skippedCount); one that fails is logged by its order and the rest go on, and the run's time and counts are kept on the watermark "attribution". Runs as the system.
